baseline_facts.content: Patient is 32 years old.
Patient is a medical doctor working in plastic surgery.
Patient lives with their wife.
Patient does not smoke.
Patient wears glasses.
Patient is allergic to penicillin.
Patient reports no other illnesses.
Patient has no history of mini-strokes or TIAs.
Patient has been experiencing episodic symptoms for about a month and a half to two months.
Patient has felt generally tired and weak over the past month or so.
During episodes, the patient experiences pins and needles in the right hand.
Pins and needles occur in the right hand only.
During episodes, the right arm feels weaker.
Right arm weakness lasts a few days and then returns to normal.
During episodes, the leg feels weaker.
Leg weakness occurs at the same time as arm symptoms.
A colleague noticed the patient walking differently during episodes.
Abnormal gait episodes last three or four days.
The patient sometimes feels nauseous.
The patient sometimes does not feel like doing anything.
During episodes, the patient has difficulty holding a cup of coffee.
During episodes, drinking coffee is slightly harder.
The patient does not currently have difficulty swallowing.
During episodes, the patient feels like there is something in the throat.
During episodes, the patient has no difficulty speaking.
The patient does not think they have visual problems during episodes.
Initially, episodes occurred about once a week to once a month.
Episodes are now occurring a couple of times a day.
The patient has no symptoms at present.
Outside of episodes, the patient is normally fit and well.
The patient’s father had an operation to the side of his neck to reduce stroke risk.
A previous cholesterol check was fine.
A previous diabetes check was OK.
A previous blood pressure check was OK.
The patient takes aspirin 75 milligrams once a day.
The patient started aspirin after the father’s operation.
The decision to take aspirin was based on information from the internet.
The patient has not informed a GP about taking aspirin.
No GP has discussed aspirin risks with the patient.
The GP’s working diagnosis is mini-stroke or TIA.
The GP will refer the patient to a TIA clinic.
The TIA clinic appointment is expected within 1 to 2 days.
The TIA clinic will perform an ultrasound of the carotid arteries.
The TIA clinic may perform a brain scan.
The patient was advised to attend A&E if symptoms return and are prolonged.
Patient had episodes of feeling very tired lasting a couple of days then returning to normal.
